subject: Business
title: Good Cop, Bad Cop in Business
description: A micro-lesson that makes Good Cop, Bad Cop in Business usable.

hook.text: One executive is aggressive. The other is friendly and apologetic. You trust the nice one. That's the trap.

buildup.text: Good cop/bad cop uses contrasting roles to pressure and then comfort the other side into concessions.

discovery.text: The bad cop raises tension. The good cop offers relief — at a price. Gratitude lowers your guard.

twist.text: It's one of the oldest tactics in negotiation. Knowing it exists is half the defense.

climax.text: Counter it by negotiating only with the decision-maker and addressing both roles as a single unit.

punchline.text: If one side is playing two roles, they have one goal.

quiz.question: How should you counter good cop/bad cop?
options: Treat both as a single team with one goal
Only talk to the nice one

details.summary: Good cop bad cop uses two negotiators where one is aggressive and the other appears sympathetic and reasonable by contrast. The bad cop pushes extreme positions, then the good cop offers a compromise that seems generous relative to the bad cop but still favors their side.
details.whyItMatters: This classic tactic works because contrast makes the good cop's offer feel like a concession even when it is not. Recognizing the pattern prevents you from accepting terms that only seem reasonable in comparison to the manufactured extreme position.
takeaways: One negotiator plays aggressive while the other appears reasonable by contrast
The contrast makes the moderate offer feel generous when it may not be
Recognizing the tactic neutralizes its effectiveness immediately

faq.question: How do you recognize good cop bad cop when it is being used against you?
faq.answer: Watch for one person consistently being unreasonable while another sympathetically pushes the same direction more gently. Notice if the good cop steers you toward terms that still heavily favor their side. The pattern is most obvious when the two people alternate predictably during discussions.

faq.question: What is the best response when you identify good cop bad cop?
faq.answer: Name it directly and calmly. Say you appreciate both perspectives but want to negotiate on the merits. Evaluate proposals against your own criteria rather than against the bad cop's extreme position. Deal only with the good cop if necessary, making the bad cop irrelevant.
